newsitem.title: INDONESIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indonesian newspapers - Jan 17.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indonesian newspapers - Jan 17.

text.p: The following are the leading stories in the Indonesian press on January 17. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
President Suharto has set up a special council to advise him on maritime affairs. He said the development of the archipelagic nation's maritime sector needed orderly planning.

Lieutenant-General Syarwan Hamid, head of the Indonesian military's socio-political section, denied recent accusations that the armed forces had been "playing with fire" by provoking recent riots and disturbances.
Leading economists and bankers have urged the government to take immediate steps to cut the burgeoning current account deficit.
Members of the House of Representatives, except those from the Moslem-orientated United Development Party (PPP), have pledged to fully support a bill on domestic futures commodity trading.

Police sources say detectives have written to President Suharto seeking the necessary permission to question legislator and ousted Indonesian Democratic Party (PDI) leader Megawati Sukarnoputri. The paper said she is accused of having illegal meetings at her Jakarta residence.

Transmigration Minister Siswono Yudhohusodo reported to President Suharto about recent comments he made that the nation and government were "sick". State Secretary Murdiono said Yudhohusodo told Suharto he had been misquoted.
Lieutenant-General Syarwan Hamid said that recent ethnic and religious riots were not carried out by Islamic fundamentalists but by an unnamed group using an "old format".
